newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria reiterates refineries, oil joint ventures.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria reiterates refineries, oil joint ventures.

text.p: Nigeria's military government reiterated on Monday that it is seriously considering selling its oil joint ventures and also intends to privatise its refineries.

"Joint Venture Operations: Government is giving serious consideration to selling its 57 percent equity shares in these projects to private investors," Finance Minister Anthony Ani told a seminar in Lagos on attracting foreign investment into the country.
Nigeria's oil industry is currently run by multinational companies in joint ventures with state-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC).
Among these are Royal Dutch Shell Group, Mobil Corp, Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc.
Others are Elf Aquitaine and Agip SpA.
"Government also intends to privatise the refineries after an evaluation of the current value of each of them," Ani said.
Nigeria's four refineries run at a fraction of their combined output capacity of 445,000 barrels per day because of poor management and fraud.
Industry experts say that if properly run, the refineries could supply a large market in West and Central Africa.
Ani said the government was also willing to grant licences to competent private investors to set up export-oriented refineries in Nigeria.
The World Bank and the private sector have long been urging Nigeria to revive its economy by privatising key sectors such as electricity, petroleum and telecommunications.
Nigeria's economy is one of Africa's biggest but has been bedevilled by political instability, foreign debt of more than $32 billion and long-term falling income from its main export, crude oil.
Ani said: "The government is willing to tailor incentives to match the specific needs of foreign investors which can be negotiated."
"Virtually every sector of the economy is conducive to foreign investment."
